title: CDKN1A promotes Cis-induced AKI by inducing cytoplasmic ROS production and ferroptosis.
authors: Gao, Qian; Chen, Jun-Ming; Li, Chen-Sui-Zi; Zhan, Jia-Yi; Yin, Xue-Dong; Li, Ben-Shang; Dong, Hong-Liang; Luo, Lian-Xiang; Li, Zhi-Ling
journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CDKN1A在顺铂诱导急性肾损伤中的作用机制，属于疾病病理与细胞实验，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: This study focuses on investigating the role of CDKN1A in cisplatin-induced AKI (acute kidney injury, AKI) and its potential as a biomarker for early diagnosis and therapeutic intervention by integrating bioinformatics analysis, machine learning, and experimental validation. METHODS: We analyzed the GSE85957 dataset to find genes that changed between control and cisplatin-treated rats. Using bioinformatics and machine learning, we found 13 important genes related to ferroptosis and the P53 pathway. The key gene, CDKN1A, was identified using various algorithms. We then tested how reducing CDKN1A in human kidney cells affected cell health, ROS, and iron levels. We also checked how CDKN1A changes the levels of proteins linked to ferroptosis using Q-PCR and Western Blot. RESULTS: CDKN1A was found to negatively regulate the G1/S phase transition and was associated with ferroptosis in p53 signaling. Experiments in human renal tubular epithelial cells (HK-2) and rat NRK-52E cells showed that CDKN1A knockdown mitigated cisplatin-induced cell injury by reducing oxidative stress and ferroptosis. CONCLUSION: Our integrated approach identified CDKN1A as a biomarker for cisplatin-induced AKI. Its regulation could be key in AKI pathogenesis, offering new therapeutic insights and aiding in early diagnosis and intervention.
abstract_zh: 背景与目的：本研究通过整合生物信息学分析、机器学习及实验验证，探讨CDKN1A在顺铂诱导的急性肾损伤（acute kidney injury, AKI）中的作用，并评估其作为早期诊断及治疗干预生物标志物的潜力。方法：我们分析了GSE85957数据集，以寻找对照组与顺铂处理大鼠之间发生变化的基因。利用生物信息学和机器学习，我们发现了13个与铁死亡（ferroptosis）及P53通路相关的重要基因。通过多种算法，确定了关键基因CDKN1A。随后，我们检测了在人肾细胞中敲低CDKN1A对细胞活力、活性氧（ROS）及铁水平的影响，并使用Q-PCR和Western Blot检查了CDKN1A对铁死亡相关蛋白水平的变化。结果：CDKN1A被发现负向调控G1/S期转换，并与p53信号中的铁死亡相关。在人肾小管上皮细胞（HK-2）和大鼠NRK-52E细胞中的实验表明，CDKN1A敲低通过减少氧化应激和铁死亡，减轻了顺铂诱导的细胞损伤。结论：我们的整合方法将CDKN1A确定为顺铂诱导AKI的生物标志物。其调控可能在AKI发病机制中起关键作用，为治疗提供新见解，并有助于早期诊断和干预。
